title: Set a git repository's own user.email in the terminal

capabilities.why: Xfce's terminal and git, and xdotool, which setup places the window with.
argv: command -v xfce4-terminal && command -v git && command -v xdotool

setup.why: Make a git repository whose own user.email is the old address, and keep the global user.email as it was before the run (empty when none is set), which a check compares.

argv: d=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; rm -rf $d && mkdir -p $d && git init -q $d/repo-{{nonce}} && git -C $d/repo-{{nonce}} config user.email {{who.old}} && { git config --global --get user.email || true; } > $d/global-email-before

setup.why: Open Xfce's terminal in the run's folder, its pid kept beside the folder so teardown stops this terminal and no other.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && echo $$ > /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-terminal.pid && exec xfce4-terminal --disable-server --working-directory=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}

setup.why: Wait for the terminal's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, put the pointer on it and activate it: a window manager gives the keys to the window activated, and with none they go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class xfce4-terminal | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no terminal window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); xdotool windowactivate $w 2>/dev/null; sleep 1

instruction: In the terminal window, set the user.email of the git repository /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/repo-{{nonce}} to {{who.new}}, for that repository only (not your global git config).

checks.why: The repository's own config (git config --local) says the new address. Setup set it to {{who.old}} there, which a global setting can't override, so an agent that does nothing fails, and so does one that sets it only globally.
The global user.email is what it was before the run: an agent that also sets it globally, which the instruction forbids, fails.
argv: [ "$(git config --global --get user.email)" = "$(cat /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/global-email-before)" ] && echo kept || echo changed

teardown.why: Close the run's terminal (by the pid setup kept: a desktop may have other terminals open) and delete the run's folder.

argv: for f in /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; do [ -f "$f" ] && kill -9 "$(cat "$f")" 2>/dev/null; done; rm -f /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; rm -rf /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; true

oracle.why: Type the command into the terminal and run it.
